 Judgment

The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Additional MACT and Additional Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Bidar (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.268/2017 vide its judgment and award dated 03.07.2020.
2.

The claimant, aged 39 years and employed in a private company suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 02.06.2011 when a lorry bearing registration No.GJ-03/W-8821 (henceforth referred to as 'offending vehicle') knocked him down.
The claimant suffered injuries to the head, abdomen and shoulder and fell unconscious.
The claimant was shifted to Government Hospital, Mannaekhelli in an unconscious state, from where he was referred to Government Hospital, Bidar.
He was treated as an inpatient for a period of 3 days and thereafter he was treated at Gangamai Institute of Neuro Sciences, where he was admitted as an inpatient on 05.06.2011.
The claimant claimed that he availed treatment at a Hospital at Sholapur and was discharged on 18.06.2011.

He contended that he was drawing monthly salary of Rs.15,000/-
NC: 2023:KHC-K:5515 and due to the injuries, he was disabled and could not concentrate on the work and thus was deprived of the ability to earn his livelihood.
He therefore, filed a claim petition claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
3. The claim petition was resisted by the insurer who denied the accident as well as the entitlement of the claimant for the compensation.
It alleged that the claimant had conspired with the local police to charge sheet the driver of the offending vehicle.
It contended that the claimant tried to cross the road without observing the moving traffic and thereby contributed to the accident.
Thus, it contended that it was the claimant who was negligent and not the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the claimant was not entitled to any compensation.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P27.
He examined a doctor as PW.2 who deposed that the claimant had suffered several injuries and that these injuries had resulted in severe neurological NC: 2023:KHC-K:5515 complications.
It assessed the disability suffered by the claimant at 42% to the whole body.
PW.3 was the employer of the claimant who deposed that the claimant was paid salary of Rs.12,000/- per month.
However, the insurer did not lead any evidence.
5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

It held that the claimant had Syed Pasha S/O Amiruddin vs Keshubhai Wo Rahyabhai Dhankeha And Anr on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77372061/
2 suffered injuries in the accident.

sentences.text: However, it did not consider the evidence of PW.2 that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 42% to the whole body as PW.2 was not the doctor who treated the claimant.

The Tribunal considered the income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.5,000/- per month and his age as 31 years and awarded the following compensation:-
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Pain and sufferings 30,000/-
 2 Medical attendant and other 18,000/-
 incidental charges

3 Loss of laid up period charges 15,000/-
 4 Medical charges 77,733/-
 5 Loss of basic amenities 30,000/-
 Total 1,70,733/-
 NC: 2023:KHC-K:5515
The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization.
6. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant is in appeal.

7. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that as per the disability certificate at Ex.P10, the claimant had suffered following complications due to the injuries:-
1. Loss of smell.
2. No taste over tongue.
3. Deafness in R-ear.
4. Salivation from R-side in sleep.
5. Weakness in R-upper arm.
6. Headache on laughing.
7.
On and off giddiness and reeling sensation.
8. Lethargy, heaviness in head, confusion, forgetfulness, etc.,
The learned counsel submitted that the assessment of disability by PW.2 deserves to be accepted.

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned counsel or the insurer contended that PW.2 was not the doctor, who treated the claimant and was not medically qualified to assess neurological NC: 2023:KHC-K:5515 complications resulting from the injuries.
He submitted that the only injury that the claimant suffered was bilateral hemorrhagic contusion with cerebral edema, which required conservative treatment and did not result in any disability.
He therefore, contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper as the Tribunal awarded compensation for the loss of income during the laid up period.
He further submitted that the claimant did not produce any material to show that he had not attended work after the laid up period.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.
10. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the insurer, the claimant had suffered blunt injury on his abdomen and head injury.
The bilateral hemorrhagic contusion with cerebral edema did not result in any disability though it could have resulted in pain and agony apart from some discomfort.

The evidence of PW.2 that the claimant had suffered various neurological disorders is without any basis as PW.2 was not NC: 2023:KHC-K:5515 qualified to issue a certificate of neurological disability.
This Court has seen that PW.2 has in many a case given false disability certificate and this Court has referred the case of PW.2 to the Karnataka Medical council.

Therefore,
in the absence of any other corresponding material to indicate that the claimant had suffered neurological disability as mentioned in Ex.P10, the assessment of disability by PW.2 cannot be taken into consideration for the purpose of calculating the disability suffered by the claimant.

Having regard to the fact that the claimant was admitted in a Government Hospital for a period of 3 days and thereafter in a private hospital, where he was treated for nearly 10 days, this Court would consider it appropriate to globally enhance the compensation by a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-.
11. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.1,70,733/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.2,70,733/-, which is payable by the insurer of the offending vehicle along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
13. Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
